Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.
data.title: Standup: separate auto-dispatched from manually dispatched items in 'Yesterday I completed work on...'

# Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner

**Origin:** `discovered-from:OSL-0MVMCP5DT005PIFS` (filed from ContentCreator; that item was deleted once this one existed and was synced).

**Headline:** The framework's v3 pre-push hook refuses every `dev`/`main` push unless the pushed repo ships its own `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, so `install_pi.sh` still ships a gate-less v2 hook to every project without one. Make v3 resolve the runner local-then-global (the pattern the same file already uses for the context-budget gate), ship v3 everywhere, and upgrade stale installed copies.

## Problem statement

Only the SorraAgents checkout contains `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; every other project receives its skills from the global install at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. The v3 hook's full-suite gate looks for the runner at `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only, so in every non-SorraAgents repo the gate hard-fails (`exit 1`) on any push to `dev`/`main`. `scripts/install_pi.sh` works around that by installing `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — a hook **without** the full-suite gate — into every project that lacks a repo-local runner. The result is two hook variants, and the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee is absent from every project except SorraAgents itself.

The cost is visible: `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` had to hand-write a local-then-global runner lookup into ContentCreator's hook (its only deviation from the framework's) before the full-suite push gate could be restored there.

## Users

- **Agents pushing to `dev`** in any framework project — they need the same push-time guarantee everywhere, not only in SorraAgents.
- **The operator / producer** — one hook to audit, one documented contract, no per-repo fork to drift.
- **Project maintainers running `install_pi.sh`** — a fresh install must not choose a weaker hook, and a stale installed hook must not silently keep the weaker one.

Example user stories:

- As an agent pushing to `dev` in a project with no repo-local `skill/` tree, I want the full suite to run through the global runner, so a red tree is refused before it reaches the shared branch.
- As a maintainer, I want `install_pi.sh` to install one hook for every project, so I never have to reason about which variant my repo received.
- As the operator, I want an incomplete install to refuse the push and name the bypass, rather than silently skipping the gate.

## Desired change

1. **Runner resolution (v3 hook).** Resolve the runner local-then-global inside the full-suite gate, mirroring the context-budget block in the same file:
   - `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present;
   - else `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`;
   - when neither exists, fail closed and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (unchanged fail-closed stance, better message).
   This makes the framework hook converge with the block ContentCreator already runs (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` AC2), so the project copy can eventually be deleted rather than forked.
2. **One hook variant.** `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook in every project — the `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` precondition is dropped and `.githooks/pre-push.v2` is removed (or reduced to a pointer note), with the hook-selection comments and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` corrected to describe reality.
3. **Installed-hook upgrade.** `install_pi.sh` must no longer leave a stale installed `.githooks/pre-push` in place forever: when the file's revision marker is a framework revision older than the current one **and the file is an unmodified framework copy**, replace it (backup the previous file, report what happened); when the file carries local modifications, report it and leave it alone. Re-running is idempotent (no rewrite when already current).
4. **Documentation.** The hook contract, the runner resolution order, the revision markers and the upgrade path are documented in the framework docs (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, plus a hook section or `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` mirroring the project-side doc), and the hook header comment states the resolution order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Global runner resolution:** with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` but a global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, a `refs/heads/dev` push through the v3 hook executes the global runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env` from the pushed repo's root, and a green run permits the push (regression test, fake global runner).

# implement.py parent: terminal blockers still gate topological readiness

discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` builds its dependency graph from **every** in-chain
dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is already terminal, so a
finished blocker still occupies the topological ordering and delays — or in
practice starves — the genuinely ready child that depends on it. A child whose
blockers are all terminal is *ready now*, yet it can be sorted behind unrelated
children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high `sortIndex`.

## Users

- **Primary — agent/operator running an epic:** "As the agent driving an epic
  with `implement.py parent`, I want a child whose blockers are all already
  finished to be selected as soon as it is the lowest-sorting ready child, so
  in-flight implementation work is never skipped and I never have to finish it
  manually."
- **Secondary — producer/reviewer:** "As a producer, I want the reported
  implementation order to mean 'blockers first, then sortIndex', so I can
  predict which child the next run will start."
- **Maintainer:** "As a maintainer, I want the ordering fix covered by a
  regression test with the exact shape that broke, so the readiness rule
  cannot silently regress."

## Observed failure (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

Resolved order for the epic's 8 children:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

`K0V4` (sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound `depends-on`
edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex 8100). `O53Z` was
already `completed`, so `K0V4` should have been ready immediately; instead it
was released only after `O53Z`'s slot near the end of the queue.

Consequences:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4` although its
   worktree held a completed in-flight implementation — it returned
   "start child VDA9"; the in-flight work had to be finished manually with
   `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not "blockers first" in any intuitive sense: a ready
   child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its finished
   blocker sorted late.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Terminal blockers never gate readiness.** In
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` an in-chain dependency edge whose blocker
   is terminal — `_is_terminal_child()` is true: status in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`
   (`in_review`, `completed`, `done`, `deleted`) or the item is soft-deleted —
   contributes neither to `in_degree[child]` nor to `dependents[blocker]`. The
   graph is therefore built over non-terminal children only, and a child whose
   in-chain blockers are all terminal is in the **initial** ready set.
2. **Ready children are ordered by their own `(sortIndex, id)`.** For the
   reproduction shape (open child `LOW` with sortIndex 3000 whose only in-chain
   blocker is a `completed` child `HIGH` with sortIndex 8100, plus an unrelated
   open child `MID` with sortIndex 5000) the resolved order starts with `LOW`,
   then `MID`, then `HIGH` — i.e. `LOW`'s position is decided by its own
   `sortIndex`, never by its blocker's.
3. **Regression test reproduces the exact shape.** A new
   `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` covers at
   minimum: (a) the reproduction shape above, asserting `LOW` is **first**;
   (b) an all-terminal children set, asserting ordering is purely
   `(sortIndex, id)`; (c) a non-terminal chain `A ← B` (both open), asserting
   `A` precedes `B` (real blocking still respected); (d) a soft-deleted blocker
   treated as terminal; (e) an external blocker (id not among the children)
   creating no edge; (f) the existing cycle path still returning
   `([], error)` with the cyclic children named; (g) `_next_child_to_implement`
   still refusing a child whose in-chain blocker is **non**-terminal. The
   reproduction test must be shown red against the pre-fix source and green
   after the fix.
4. **No change to adjacent behaviour.** Cycle detection (fail-fast, no infinite
   recursion), cross-project/external-blocker reporting, `_classify_child`
   (`skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress`) and the blocked-child guard in
   `_next_child_to_implement` are unchanged, and the parent still advances once
   every child is terminal.
5. **Documentation updated.** The
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` docstring states the readiness rule
   (terminal blockers are pre-satisfied), and the parent-recursion/dependency
   ordering text in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (plus any `docs/dev/*` reference
   that describes the ordering) is updated to match; code comments explain why
   terminal edges are excluded.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — the
   implement-skill group (`pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`) is green and the
   full suite (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`) passes on the
   committed tip.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code is agent infrastructure owned by **SorraAgents**:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout contains no `skill/` tree). The item
  was relocated here from the AI_Hell worklog (AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6) by producer
  decision, following the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent, while keeping its
  `discovered-from` link to the AI_Hell epic that exposed the defect. The change,
  its tests, docs, commit and full-suite evidence therefore all stay inside this
  repo — `implement.py start <id>` from this checkout creates the worktree here
  and `wl` resolves this store, so no cross-store resolution is involved.
- **Explicit authorisation to edit `skill/`.** The repository-boundary rule
  forbids editing `skill/` unless explicitly instructed; this work item *is*
  that instruction, scoped to the files listed under **Key Files**.
- **Determinism preserved.** Tie-break stays `(sortIndex, id)`; no
  non-deterministic iteration order (sets are always sorted before use).
- **Narrow scope.** Do **not** change `wl dep` semantics, `sortIndex`
  generation/assignment, child classification, or the `parent` phase's broader
  control flow.
- **No new runtime dependencies;** Python 3.8+ compatible; stdlib only (as the
  existing module is).

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review", "completed", "done", "deleted"}` (~line
  769), `_is_terminal_status()` (~772), `_is_terminal_child()` (~784, also
  treats a soft-deleted `deletedBy` child as terminal).
- `_classify_child()` (~810) — `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`.
- `_resolve_implementation_order(children, blockers)` (~836) — Kahn's
  algorithm; today:

  ```python
  for edge in blockers.get(cid, []):
      bid = str(edge.get("id", ""))
      if bid in child_ids:              # <-- terminal blockers still counted
          in_degree[cid] += 1
          dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  The ready queue is `sorted(... in_degree[cid] == 0 ..., key=(sortIndex, id))`
  and is re-sorted after each release, so a terminal blocker with a high
  `sortIndex` delays its dependent.
- `_next_child_to_implement(children, blockers_map)` (~905) already gates on
  *non-terminal* in-chain blockers (`all(bid in terminal_ids ...)`), so the
  guard and the sort currently disagree — the inconsistency this item fixes.
- Caller `phase_parent` (~5124) calls `_resolve_implementation_order()` and
  returns early on a cycle error; `_next_child_to_implement()` then picks from
  the ordered list.
- Tests live in `skill/implement/tests/` (6 files, `.pi/test-config.json` group
  `implement` → `pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`); **no test currently covers
  `_resolve_implementation_order` or `_next_child_to_implement` directly.**

## Desired change

- Skip terminal blockers when building the graph in
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` — e.g.

  ```python
  if bid in child_ids and not _is_terminal_child(child_by_id[bid]):
      in_degree[cid] += 1
      dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  (equivalently: collapse terminal children out of the graph before the sort).
  Terminal children remain present in the returned order so the caller still
  reports/finishes them, and their own placement is still decided by their own
  `(sortIndex, id)`.
- Cycle detection then operates over the non-terminal subgraph only; keep the
  same error message/format and the fail-fast return.
- Update the docstring (readiness rule + why terminal edges are excluded) and
  the ordering documentation in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Add the regression test module described in AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**:
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` graph construction + docstring;
  `_next_child_to_implement()` docstring cross-reference if needed.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` (SorraAgents) —
  **New**: ordering/readiness regression tests (AC3), including the red-then-
  green reproduction shape.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**: parent-recursion /
  dependency-order text states that terminal blockers do not gate readiness.
- `docs/dev/*` in SorraAgents — **Edit (if present)**: any ordering description
  that contradicts the new rule (verify with
  `grep -rn "topological\|dependency order" docs/ skill/implement/`).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Masking a real cycle.* Excluding terminal blockers from the graph could hide
  a cycle that passes through a terminal child. Mitigation: a cycle can only
  block work that still needs doing, so detection over the non-terminal
  subgraph is the correct semantics; document it in the docstring and cover it
  with AC3(f) (cycle among non-terminal children still fails fast).
- *Accidental behaviour drift elsewhere.* `_next_child_to_implement()` has its
  own terminal-aware guard; the fix must align with it rather than replace it.
  Mitigation: AC3(g) asserts the guard still refuses non-terminal-blocked
  children; AC4 forbids changing adjacent paths.
- *Cross-repo verification gap.* The AI_Hell audit/CI cannot see SorraAgents
  files, so a green AI_Hell report does not prove the fix. Mitigation: run the
  implement-skill pytest group and the SorraAgents full suite from the
  SorraAgents worktree and record the evidence (red/green, commit hash) on this
  item, per AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- *Test-gate selection.* Changed-scope selection may not see the new test file
  until it is tracked; Mitigation: `git add` before the gate run and confirm the
  `implement` group is selected (otherwise fall back to full scope).
- *Scope creep.* The 2026-10-23 report also notes the confusing reported order
  generally and the manual `finish K0V4` step; richer ordering diagnostics or
  `parent`-phase rework are **not** in scope. Mitigation: record follow-ups as
  separate items (see Related work) rather than widening this fix.

**Assumptions**

- The item now lives in the **SorraAgents** worklog (relocated from AI_Hell by
  producer decision, per the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent); the AI_Hell epic
  AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S remains recorded as the origin via `discovered-from`.
- Terminal blockers are pre-satisfied for *ordering* purposes but are still
  reported in the resolved order (existing `skip-terminal` classification
  handles them in the loop), so no caller contract changes.
- Soft-deleted children behave as terminal for this rule (they can never be
  implemented) — consistent with `_is_terminal_child()`.

## Related work

Cross-repo (SorraAgents — the code's owning repo; automated `find-related`
searched only the AI_Hell store because the item's prefix pins that store, and
its file matches are noise here):

- **SA-0MSQIJBTB008RHS1** — *completed* — V2: Dependency-graph resolution,
  topological ordering & cycle detection; the change that introduced
  `_resolve_implementation_order()`.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** — *completed* — implement skill: `/skill:implement
  <parent-id>` must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain;
  defined the in-chain/external blocker split and the blocked-child guard.
- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — *open* — implement.py parent ignores the
  do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child; same selection path
  (`_next_child_to_implement`), different rule. **Relocated** from the AI_Hell
  worklog because `implement.py` is SorraAgents-owned — the precedent for the
  OPEN QUESTION below.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — *completed* — implement skill: drive all epic
  children to completion (fresh session per child); the `parent`/`drive` flow

### Goal

Extend the in-repo, fail-open Herdr CLI helper with a session-level pane/agent
boundary and provide a deterministic recording **fake** Herdr CLI, so the pane
transport and its tests can exercise `pane split` / `agent start` /
`agent prompt` / `agent wait` / `pane close` without a live Herdr.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive runs `pane split` (no `tab create`/`workspace create`) with `--cwd`, started via `agent start` and prompted via `agent prompt --wait`; asserted by a fake-CLI test.
- A recording fake Herdr CLI (test-only shim plus in-process runner with scripted responses) lets tests assert exact herdr invocations (arguments and order) and simulate `done`, `blocked`, `timeout`, `agent_not_ready` and CLI-failure transitions with no live Herdr.
- Agent names `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` are validated against herdr's `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` rule with deterministic truncation; unit tests cover valid, truncated and collision cases.
- `agent start` requiring an interactive shell prompt is handled: `agent_not_ready` is retried within the configured wait budget or surfaced as a reported reason — never a crash.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- **Forked-decision resolution (intake Appendix):** keep the boundary in
  `skill/shared/` and reuse `herdr_pane.py`'s `HERDR_BIN_PATH` resolution,
  subprocess env handling and fail-open return style — do not duplicate that
  logic. Additive changes only to in-repo files; no edits to repo-external
  herdr skill or `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`.
- Surface (one injectable client, every call returning a parsed result or a
  fail-open `{"success": false, "reason": ...}`, never raising):
  `pane split --current --cwd <path> [--env K=V] [--focus|--no-focus]`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve --no-extensions`,
  `agent prompt <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`,
  `agent wait <name> --until done|blocked`, `pane close <id>`,
  `pane rename <id> <label>`.
- Parse ids defensively from `.result.pane.pane_id` and agent JSON; treat
  unknown shapes as a reported failure (Herdr API-drift mitigation).
- Fake CLI lives under the tests tree (`skill/shared/tests/`), scripted by the
  test, emitting JSON matching the real CLI shape.

- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`
- `skill/shared/herdr_session.py` (new, if split out)

None — foundation slice; blocks the spawner and lifecycle slices.

  rename) reusing `herdr_pane.py` conventions.
- Recording fake Herdr CLI + fixtures.
- Unit tests, all green, no live Herdr needed.
- Short reference-doc note for the helper.

transport per invocation: pane driving only when Herdr is detected **and** the

### Goal

Drive the pane-side lifecycle to completion in `phase_drive`: wait on session
state (never process exit), report blocked children, bound the wait with the
existing timeouts, and close or explicitly retain every pane — with additive
report parity for human and `--json` output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child is decided by `agent wait --until done|blocked` plus the `phase_parent` stage re-read; tests cover done, blocked, timeout.
- **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent reports `blocked`, drive stops, records `blocked_child`/`blocked_pane`, leaves the pane open and names it.
- **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once its child reaches a terminal stage or (b) retained and reported; tests assert close per success and no close when blocked.
- **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.** `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` and `--max-child-sessions` still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane and stops the chain.
- **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport`; the summary lists retained panes, asserted by tests.
- **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Implementation notes

- `phase_parent` stays the authority for terminality; the `agent wait` result
  is only a fast-path/stop signal. Reuse `_reconcile_spawn_failure` so a child
  that reached a terminal stage before the wait expired is still reported as
  `completed-late`, not failed.
- `blocked` → report keys `blocked_child` / `blocked_pane`, a `retained_panes`
  entry, and an actionable message naming the pane (e.g.
  `herdr pane read <pane_id>`); title the pane via
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` (`⚠️`/`🚫` verdicts).
- Close path: `pane close <id>` after the child's terminal stage is confirmed;
  retain on blocked/failed with a verdict title. Never leak silently.
- `_emit_phase_report` gains additive keys only; the human rendering appends a
  "panes retained for inspection" list. Existing deterministic orchestration
  tests (`ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`) keep passing unchanged.
- Timeout behaviour keeps today's semantics: close the pane, record `reason`,
  stop the chain (reconciled against the child's real stage first).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`phase_drive`, `_emit_phase_report`)
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (Step 6.1)

## Dependencies

- Pane session spawner and opt-in transport selection.

## Deliverables

- done / blocked / timeout lifecycle handling with `phase_parent` authority.
- Close-or-retain rule with pane-title verdicts.
- Report fields (`pane_id`, `transport`, blocked/retained panes) plus human
  rendering, with parity tests.
- Doc updates for blocked-child handling and retained panes.

## Goal

Replace the whole-directory `node_modules` symlink in `implement.py start` with a **worktree-local link farm** so workspace packages resolve to the worktree's own source tree. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

`_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (~L1695 in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main-checkout>/node_modules`. ## Goal

Make `implement.py finish` **fail closed** when a worktree changes `packages/shared/src/**` while `@worklog/shared` still resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — an actionable error naming the stale path and remediation, so a green gate never silently passes on the wrong code. Parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO.

## Problem (parent: SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO)

`phase_finish` runs build → test gate → commit from the worktree. If resolution is stale (worktree's `@worklog/shared` → main checkout's `packages/shared/dist`), the gate either false-reds on correct new code (WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO) or false-greens on broken code. The gate currently cannot distinguish "shared code changed in this worktree" from "shared code unchanged" and exposes no resolution diagnostic.

## Desired change (producer-decided: hard-fail)

1. Extract the resolution check from the F2 link-farm feature into a shared helper (`@worklog/shared` resolved package root == `<worktree>/packages/shared`), reused by the `start` JSON report and `finish`.
2. In `phase_finish`, before the test gate (after the build step), compute whether the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` and whether the resolution check fails; when both hold, hard-fail with a message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation (re-run `implement.py start` / the documented refresh command from the main checkout, then rebuild).
3. End-to-end probe verification (AC1): in a fresh worktree, a probe change under `packages/shared/src/**` is observed by the sanctioned gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`), and an unmodified main checkout would not observe it.
4. Detection no-ops for repos without a workspace shared package (degradation path).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `finish` hard-fails (non-zero, no commit, item released to `open` with the failure comment) with an actionable message naming the stale `<main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist` path and the remediation when the worktree diff touches `packages/shared/src/**` AND the resolution check fails — covered by the F1 negative-path test.
2. The gate passes normally when the resolution check succeeds (worktree-local link farm present), including when shared source is unchanged.
3. The e2e probe proves the worktree's `packages/shared/src/**` change is observed by the gate (`run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) from inside a fresh worktree, and that an unmodified main checkout does not observe it.
4. The resolution helper is shared between `start` and `finish` (single source of truth), and its detection logic is covered by the F1 unit tests.
5. No change to main-checkout build/test behaviour (byte-for-byte unchanged outside worktree setups); the main checkout stays git-clean of non-gitignored artefacts after start → build → gate → finish.

- **Traceability (parent AC4):** **Hard-fail on stale resolution.** `implement.py finish` (build → test gate)
## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_stale_shared_resolution.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_node_modules_link_farm.py`

## Related

- Parent SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO; F2 link-farm dependency; false-red case WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO (ContextHub); predecessor verification WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2 / SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B.

# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.

data.description:
# Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across passing re-audits; flag failing audits for producer review

**Headline:** The audit runner must stop re-arming `needsProducerReview` on a
passing re-audit of an item the producer has already reviewed, and must start
setting it on any failing (`Ready to close: No`) top-level audit — so a
producer's review survives a release-time re-audit while genuine failures
always reach the producer queue.

## Problem statement

On 2026-10-27 a `dev`→`main` release of the ContextHub store was blocked
because the audit runner re-flagged 14 top-level `in_review` items for producer
review. The producer had already reviewed and cleared those items; the release's
own re-audits all **passed**, and each pass unconditionally wrote
`--needs-producer-review yes`, silently discarding the producer's review.
Inversely, the failing-verdict path only flags an item when
`merge_gate_blocker` is set, so genuinely failing items never reach the
producer-review queue. The review state is unobservable after the fact because
`needsProducerReview` is a bare boolean and flag-only flips neither bump
`updatedAt` nor leave any record.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — the person who reviews and clears items before
  release. *"As a producer I want a review I have given to stay given until the
  item's content actually changes, so that I am not asked to re-approve the same
  unchanged work every time a release re-audits it."*
- **Producer, failure path** — *"As a producer I want every item whose audit says
  `Ready to close: No` surfaced to me, so that a failing item cannot sit
  silently in the actionable queue."*
- **Release gate (ship skill)** — *"As the release gate I want
  `needsProducerReview` to mean exactly 'this item needs producer attention now',
  so that the gate neither blocks on already-reviewed work nor passes
  unreviewed/unready work."*
- **Audit runner (agent)** — *"As the audit runner I want an unambiguous rule for
  when to set the flag, so that pass/fail lifecycles stay deterministic and
  auditable."*

## Target behaviour

| Verdict | Item | Prior producer review (signal present) | `needsProducerReview` after the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | yes (reviewed, content unchanged since review) | **left `false`** (do not re-flag) |
| `Ready to close: Yes` | top-level | no (never reviewed, or content changed since review) | **`yes`** (current behaviour) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level (independent audit) | either | **`yes`** (generalise the merge-gate branch) |
| `Ready to close: No` | top-level, cascade-demotion-suppressed (parent-triggered re-audit of an `in_review`/`done` item) | either | **unchanged / never set** (producer decision, Q2 = no) |
| any | child (has parent) | either | **unchanged / never set** (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H) |

> **Cascade rule (producer decision Q2 = no).** A `No` produced by a
> parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item is not
> an independent review: the demotion is suppressed (SA-0MUJAPC680078396) and the
> flag is likewise left untouched. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the
> item to the producer.

Existing lifecycle guarantees are unchanged: pre-audit status/stage restore on
abort and on infrastructure failure, `updatedAt = auditedAt` on audit persist,
assignee clear-on-terminal, and the descendant cascade authorised only by a
verified `Yes`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (reviewed pass is preserved).** A passing verdict (`Ready to close: Yes`)
  on a top-level item whose producer has already reviewed it (and whose content
  is unchanged since that review) does not write
  `--needs-producer-review yes`; the stored `false` is preserved and the item is
  not re-entered into the producer-review queue.
- **AC2 (first pass still enters the queue).** A passing verdict on a top-level
  item that has never been reviewed still sets `needsProducerReview = yes`.
- **AC3 (independent failures always surface).** A failing verdict
  (`Ready to close: No`) from an **independent** audit of a top-level item sets
  `needsProducerReview = yes` regardless of whether `merge_gate_blocker` is set,
  and never clears an existing review. The single exception is the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed branch (Q2 = no): a parent-triggered re-audit of an
  already-`in_review`/`done` item leaves the flag untouched.
- **AC4 (signal is durable, auditable and content-scoped).** The review state used
  by AC1/AC3 distinguishes *"reviewed and cleared"* from *"never flagged"*, is
  recorded somewhere a later run (and a human) can inspect, and is invalidated
  when the item's reviewed content changes — so a materially changed item
  requires a fresh producer review.
- **AC5 (transitions covered by tests in the default suite).** Regression tests
  cover all four transitions — never-reviewed pass → flagged; reviewed pass →
  preserved; fail → flagged (with and without `merge_gate_blocker`); review →
  content change → pass → flagged again — plus the child exemption (AC6), the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed `No` → **unchanged** (Q2), and "`wl audit-show`
  unavailable ⇒ flagged" (fail-safe) — and run in the default suite
  (`skill/audit/tests/`, no marker gating).
- **AC6 (children unchanged).** A passing verdict on a child item never sets
  `needsProducerReview`, and no child-item lifecycle behaviour changes.
- **AC7 (no lifecycle regressions).** The existing guarantees hold: pre-audit
  status/stage restore on abort and infrastructure failure, `updatedAt =
  auditedAt` on audit persist, assignee clear-on-terminal, cascade-demotion
  suppression, and the lifecycle readback verification.
- **AC8 (docs).** The audit skill's reference documentation
  (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` lifecycle section)
  states the pass/fail flag semantics explicitly, including that producer review
  is **content-scoped** and how a cleared flag is distinguished from a
  never-flagged item.
- **AC9 (documentation currency).** All related documentation **in this
  repository** is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and `docs/dev/` entries. ContextHub's `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` is out of
  scope — this item makes no cross-repo change (see *Key Files*).
- **AC10 (suite).** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Review-state signal — DECIDED: Option B+ (producer, 2026-10-28)

`needsProducerReview` alone cannot answer *"was this reviewed?"*. Two candidate
designs were carried into intake; the seed context marked Option A as preferred,
but the repository evidence gathered during intake changed the cost/benefit
picture (see *Existing state*), so the choice was put to the producer
(Appendix Q1). **Producer chose Option B+** — inference with the persisted-report
recap. Option A-lite remains a possible later upgrade but is **not** part of this
item's scope; it does not need to be raised as a dependency.

### Option B+ — infer from existing state, recap in the persisted report (no cross-repo change) — CHOSEN

At audit start, capture the item's pre-audit audit record (`readyToClose` +
`fingerprint`, both already exposed by `wl audit-show --json`) alongside the
existing pre-audit `wl show` capture. Then:

- prior audit `readyToClose == 1` **and** its fingerprint equals the current
  content fingerprint **and** the item's `needsProducerReview == false`
  → the flag can only have been cleared by a producer *after* that passing
  audit of identical content → **preserve `false`**;
- otherwise (no prior audit, prior audit failed, or content changed since the
  passing audit) → **flag `yes`**;
- `needsProducerReview == true` is never cleared by the runner.

Because the audit content fingerprint is already content-scoped (schema-2
sha256 over the item's own `title` + `description`), this option satisfies AC4's
*content-scoped* requirement with no schema change. For auditability, the runner
appends an explicit metadata line to the report it persists anyway
(e.g. `Producer review: preserved (content fingerprint <fp>)` /
`Producer review: required (reason)`), so the decision is recorded in the
durable audit record.

### Option A-lite — durable review marker in the worklog store (cross-repo; NOT chosen)

Add a nullable marker (e.g. `audit_results.producer_reviewed_fingerprint` +
`producer_reviewed_at`, or `work_items.producerReviewedAt`) written whenever
`needsProducerReview` transitions `true → false`. The audit runner then compares
the stored reviewed fingerprint with the current one: equal → preserve `false`;
different/absent → flag `yes`.

This is exact and self-documenting, but it is a ContextHub worklog change:
schema migration + repair-on-open + the marker must be written on **every**
clear path (`wl reviewed <id> false`, `wl update --needs-producer-review false`
used by the ship gate's remediation text, the ship override that clears child
flags, and any future path). It also creates a cross-repo blocking dependency
for this item.

**Cost signal:** Option B+ is a single-repo change (one lifecycle region, one
helper, tests, docs); Option A-lite additionally requires a ContextHub work
item, migration, CLI surface and its own audit. Option B+ can be upgraded to
Option A-lite later without changing this item's acceptance criteria for the
pass/fail rules. **Not chosen by the producer — no ContextHub dependency is
raised by this item.**

## Constraints

- **Do not revert the pass-flag contract.** SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5 and
  SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW established that an automated pass puts a top-level item in
  the producer queue; this item refines *when*, not *whether*.
- **Never clear a review silently.** The runner may preserve `false`; it must not
  write `--needs-producer-review no` on any path.
- **Fail-safe direction.** When the review signal is ambiguous or unavailable
  (e.g. `wl audit-show` fails, legacy fingerprint-less audit), the runner must
  fall back to **flagging** (`yes`) — a spurious review request is a nuisance; a
  silently discarded review gate is a release-safety defect.
- **Bias to fewer `wl` calls.** No new per-item `wl` invocation on the hot path
  where the existing freshness gate already fetched the audit record; the
  forced path (`--force` / `--refresh-audits`) adds exactly one `wl audit-show`.
- **Children remain exempt** from the flag (SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H).
- No new user-facing CLI flags; no change to how a producer clears the flag.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — the passing-verdict lifecycle
  (~13576–13600) appends `["--needs-producer-review", "yes"]` for every
  top-level item with no reference to prior review state; the failing-verdict
  lifecycle (~13626–13660) adds the same flag **only** under
  `if ctx.merge_gate_blocker:` in the demotion branch.
- The runner already fetches everything needed for the decision: `wl show` at
  ~10247 yields `ctx.wi` (including `parentId` and `needsProducerReview`), and
  the pre-audit `original_status` / `original_stage` capture (~10238–10256) is
  the natural home for a pre-audit audit-record capture.
- `_check_audit_freshness` (~2085–2160) already runs `wl audit-show <id> --json`
  on the non-forced path and compares the stored v2 content fingerprint with the
  recomputed one — the same data Option B+ needs. The forced path
  (`--force`, `--refresh-audits`, batch drains) bypasses the gate, so an explicit
  capture is required there.
- `audit_results` (ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts` ~305–315) already stores
  `ready_to_close`, `audited_at`, `fingerprint`; `wl audit-show --json` exposes
  `fingerprint` (`src/commands/audit-result.ts`). `wl list --json` additionally
  emits a recomputed `currentFingerprint` via `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`
  (parity-tested against the Python algorithm).
- The audit content fingerprint is **item-data-only** (schema 2: sha256 over
  `title` + `description`) — comments and flag flips do not contribute, so a
  review-clear or a comment cannot invalidate a stored fingerprint.
- ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts` is a flag-only flip; the ship gate's
  remediation guidance (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` ~506–530) and
  `run-release.js` (~668–710) clear flags with `wl update <id>
  --needs-producer-review false`. A durable marker (Option A-lite) would have to
  hook **all** of these, not just `wl reviewed`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` lives in **ContextHub**, not SorraAgents (the seed's Key
  Files section lists it without a repo; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
  `skill/audit/SKILL.md` are the SorraAgents-side surfaces).
- The flag-only-flip contract ("flips of `needsProducerReview` do not bump
  `updatedAt`", `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` ~260) means `updatedAt` **cannot** be used
  as a review timestamp — it is bumped by the audit persist itself.
- Current behaviour is pinned by tests that must be updated with the fix:
  `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` (pass-with-hold cases at
  ~239, ~306, ~521, ~544), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` ~436
  (cascade pass still flags), `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py`
  (fail-flag cases ~523–700).
- The mock harness `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py`
  (`stateful_wl_side_effect`) deliberately passes `audit-show` through untouched
  — it needs a pre-audit audit-record knob so the new rules can be exercised.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

1. **Capture pre-audit audit state** next to the existing pre-audit `wl show`
   capture: `prior_audit = {readyToClose, fingerprint, auditedAt}` (reuse the
   freshness gate's fetch on the non-forced path; one `wl audit-show` otherwise).
   Capture failure ⇒ treat as "no prior audit" (fail-safe → flag).
2. **Add one predicate** (e.g. `_producer_review_preserved(wi, prior_audit)`)
   implementing the chosen signal from the *Review-state signal* section, with a
   single documented truth table. Pure function, unit-testable without the model.
3. **Passing branch**: keep `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level items
   **unless** the predicate holds, in which case append nothing (preserve the
   stored `false`). Log the decision (stderr + the persisted report line) with the
   reason and fingerprint. The rule is identical for items already at a terminal
   `done` stage (those keep their stage and only gain/lose the flag).
4. **Failing branch (independent `No`)**: emit `--needs-producer-review yes` for
   every top-level `No` verdict — merge-gate-blocked *and* ordinary `No` — keeping
   the existing merge-gate behaviour and adding the general case. Never emit `no`.
   This applies **only** when `_cascade_suppress_demotion` is false (see step 5).
5. **Unchanged branches**: infrastructure-failure restore and cascade-demotion
   suppression keep the flag untouched (no set, no clear) — record this explicitly
   in comments so a future edit does not "helpfully" flag on a timeout or a
   parent-triggered cascade. Per the producer's Q2 answer, a cascade-suppressed
   `No` does **not** flag even when `merge_gate_blocker` is set: the
   `--needs-producer-review yes` must move inside the non-suppressed demotion
   branch (a merge-gate failure that matters is re-surfaced by the next
   independent audit).
6. **Children**: no change (no flag on pass, existing behaviour elsewhere).
7. **Dry-run parity**: `--do-not-persist` still applies the flag rules; the
   persisted-report line is skipped (no report is stored).
8. **Tests** (default suite, `skill/audit/tests/`): extend the mock harness with a
   prior-audit knob, then add the four transition tests (AC5) plus child
   regression, merge-gate parity, the cascade-suppressed-`No`-does-not-flag case
   (Q2), and an "audit-show unavailable ⇒ flagged" fail-safe test.
9. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (add a "Producer-review
   flag lifecycle / content-scoped review" section) and
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85 lifecycle text), including the chosen option
   and the fail-safe rule.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — passing-verdict lifecycle (~13576–13600), failing-verdict lifecycle (~13626–13660), pre-audit capture (~10238–10256), `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint` (~2085–2230). Needs the pre-audit audit-record capture, the new predicate and both flag rules.
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — report persistence; needs the "Producer review: preserved/required" metadata line (Option B+).
- `skill/audit/tests/wl_helpers.py` — mock harness; needs a prior-audit/`audit-show` knob.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`, `test_audit_runner_review.py`, `test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — pinned expectations to update plus the new transition tests.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~35, ~85) — user-facing lifecycle description.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — implementation reference; new producer-review lifecycle section.
- **Not in scope (Option A-lite, rejected by the producer):** ContextHub `src/persistent-store.ts`, `src/commands/reviewed.ts`, `src/commands/update.ts`, `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`, `src/audit-fingerprint.ts`/`migrations/` — no worklog schema or CLI change is made by this item, and no cross-repo dependency is raised.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Decision 1 (cascade, producer Q2 = no).** A `No` verdict produced by a
  parent-triggered cascade re-audit of an already-`in_review`/`done` item does
  **not** set the flag — the flag follows the demotion: suppressed demotion ⇒ no
  flag. Only an independent `No` audit surfaces the item to the producer. Note
  this deliberately narrows the merge-gate branch too: a cascade-suppressed
  merge-gate `No` does not flag (the next independent audit re-surfaces it).
- **Assumption 1 (infrastructure failure).** An infrastructure-failure restore
  leaves `needsProducerReview` untouched (neither set nor cleared): a model
  timeout must never manufacture a producer-review request nor discard a review
  (producer Q3 = yes).
- **Assumption 2 (fail-safe).** Any ambiguity in the review signal resolves to
  *flag* (`yes`), never to *preserve* (`false`).
- **Assumption 3 (scope).** Only the audit runner's lifecycle writes the flag;
  the ship gate's own clearing/escalation paths (`check-audit-gate.js`,
  `check-final-validation.js`, `run-release.js`) are out of scope and unchanged.
- **Risk: derived signal (Option B+).** Without a stored review marker, a
  human cannot see *when* the producer reviewed, only that the flag is `false`
  over an unchanged passing audit. Mitigation: the persisted report line records
  the decision + content fingerprint, and Option B+ upgrades cleanly to Option
  A-lite later.
- **Risk: stale fixture expectations.** The current suite pins the unconditional
  flag in ≥6 places; a rushed edit could "fix" the tests instead of the
  behaviour. Mitigation: each test states which of AC1–AC6 it pins.
- **Risk: extra `wl` latency.** Mitigation: reuse the freshness gate's fetch;
  at most one added `wl audit-show` per forced audit.
- **Accepted edge (Option B+).** A flag cleared by an automated override rather
  than a human (the ship gate's child remediation, or the post-release close
  step) is indistinguishable from a human review. Both are intentional clears and
  preserving them is the correct outcome, so no attempt is made to tell them
  apart.
- **Risk: cascade failures are surfaced later, not immediately (Q2 = no).** A
  failing cascade re-audit no longer flags, so a genuine problem found only by a
  cascade pass reaches the producer at the next independent audit. Mitigation:
  the cascade run already prints its suppression notice to stderr and the
  persisted report keeps the `No` verdict visible on the item.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Related improvements spotted during implementation
  (e.g. a producer-review audit trail across the whole worklog, a
  `wl review-history` command) are recorded as separate work items, not folded
  into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (no parent) *(completed)*: narrowed the flag to top-level
  items; its child exemption is preserved by AC6.
- **SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5** — Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes'
  verdicts *(completed)*: introduced the unconditional pass flag this item
  refines.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item ready to close *(completed)*: the original contract.
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** — Update documentation for producer-review gating
  *(completed)*: the docs this item extends.
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** — merge-gate fail-closed flag on integration failure:
  the `merge_gate_blocker` branch generalised by AC3.
- **SA-0MUJAPC680078396** — cascade-audit demotion suppression (relevance:
  Decision 1 — the flag follows the demotion).
- **SA-0MVTPAV4N005WPWF** — Ship audit gates: content-fresh-but-time-stale
  audit blocks the release with reason 'Ready to close' *(completed)*: the
  same-release ship-gate defect named in the recurrence note; **out of scope**
  here (its own ship-side fix).
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT / SA-0MVIDI8E00063OOP** — audit content fingerprint and
  the item-data-only (v2) formula: the content-scoping mechanism AC4 reuses.

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** – Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for top-level items (no parent) (completed)
- **SA-0MS4TXDPR006HO2W** – Update documentation for producer-review gating (completed)
- **SA-0MVB1QFXI004T4G5** – Audit runner: set needsProducerReview on 'yes' verdicts (revert assignee-hold producer marking, keep assignee clear-on-terminal) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~220 further tokens)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~215 further tokens)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: producer, review, needsProducerReview, lifecycle (and ~192 further tokens)

## Evidence (reproduction)

1. Create a top-level item and audit it to a passing verdict → `needsProducerReview = yes` (AC2 behaviour).
2. `wl reviewed <id> false` (or `wl update <id> --needs-producer-review false`) → flag clears, `updatedAt` unchanged.
3. Re-audit the unchanged item to a passing verdict (or run the ship gate's `--refresh-audits`) → observed: `needsProducerReview` flips back to `yes` with `updatedAt == auditedAt`. Expected after the fix: stays `false`.

Inspect the flag at any point with:

```bash
wl show <id> --json | jq '{needsProducerReview: .workItem.needsProducerReview, updatedAt: .workItem.updatedAt}'
wl audit-show <id> --json | jq '.audit | {readyToClose, auditedAt, fingerprint}'
python3 skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py check-freshness <id>   # read-only probe
```

Observed on 2026-10-27 for WL-0MVK3WRY9009KV6P, WL-0MVIKRFP0005JDL8,
WL-0MVK0UO3Q002TXW6, WL-0MVMZP6A5005PB66, WL-0MVMSE2S0006L56D, WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0,
WL-0MVMSE5LN003KCPQ, WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1, WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX, WL-0MVOTIJ2U000JI44,
WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG, WL-0MVPRZU0A000TSWD, WL-0MVM92MZ50075E6B.

**Recurrence (2026-10-29, ContextHub release — second `dev`→`main` block).**
WL-0MVPRZU0A000TSWD was producer-cleared (`needsProducerReview=false`) over a
content-fresh passing audit; the ship gate re-audited it with `--force` and the
passing verdict re-armed the flag, so Step 3.6 exited 9 on already-approved work.
With current code the only escape is restoring the flag inside the gate's 30s
`AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS` window before the write makes the audit
time-stale again — i.e. a re-audited top-level item can otherwise only be
released by racing that window. Full timeline in the `ship` comment
`SA-C0MVTPLOD6000WCTS` on this item.

<!-- discovered-from: ContextHub release attempt 2026-10-27 (dev→main blocked by spurious producer-review flags) -->

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (review-state signal, blocking):** *"`needsProducerReview` alone cannot
  answer 'was this reviewed?'. Choose the review-state signal: (a) **Option B+** —
  infer from the stored passing audit + unchanged content fingerprint, and recap
  the decision in the persisted report (no cross-repo change, ~1 day); (b)
  **Option A-lite** — add a durable `producer_reviewed_at` + fingerprint marker
  written on every `true → false` transition (exact, but a ContextHub schema +
  CLI change, raising a cross-repo dependency and blocking this item)."*
  **Recommended:** Option B+ — the v2 content fingerprint already stored on
  `audit_results` makes the inference content-scoped, so AC4 is met without a
  worklog schema change or a cross-repo blocker; Option A-lite remains a clean
  later upgrade.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "b+" — Option B+ chosen.** Option A-lite is
  rejected for this item: no ContextHub schema/CLI change and no cross-repo
  dependency. Research evidence: inspected `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  lifecycle + `_check_audit_freshness`, ContextHub `src/commands/reviewed.ts`,
  `src/persistent-store.ts` `audit_results`, `src/commands/audit-result.ts`,
  `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`; summarised in *Existing state*.
- **Q2 (cascade behaviour):** *"Should a `No` verdict from a parent-triggered
  cascade re-audit of a top-level item also set the flag, even though the
  demotion is suppressed?"*
  **Recommended:** Yes — demotion suppression protects workflow position, the
  flag protects release safety.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "no" — the producer overruled the
  recommendation.** A cascade-suppressed `No` leaves `needsProducerReview`
  untouched (no flag), including when `merge_gate_blocker` is set; the flag
  follows the demotion. Implemented as Decision 1 in *Risks & assumptions* and
  as the cascade row of the *Target behaviour* table.
- **Q3 (infrastructure-failure behaviour):** *"May a timeout/infrastructure-failure
  restore leave `needsProducerReview` untouched (never set, never cleared)?"*
  **Recommended:** Yes — a transient failure must not manufacture a review
  request nor discard one.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-28): "yes" — confirmed**; recorded as Assumption 1
  in *Risks & assumptions* and step 5 of *Desired change*.

## Effort and Risk (estimated on Option B+ — the signal chosen by the producer)

- **T-shirt size:** Small
- **PERT:** O=4.50h, M=7.00h, P=13.00h → **expected 7.58h**, recommended
  **11.58h** with overheads (coordination 0.5, review 1.0, testing 1.0, risk
  buffer 1.5); range 8.50h–17.00h
- **WBS:** audit_runner lifecycle change 3.33h; regression tests + mock harness
  3.17h; documentation 1.08h
- **Risk:** score 13/25 — High (probability 3.16/5, impact 4.21/5); confidence
  74%
- **Cost of Option A-lite instead:** adds a ContextHub schema migration, CLI
  surface, cross-repo blocking dependency and its own audit — approximately
  double the effort, plus a release-ordering constraint (this item cannot land
  before the worklog change). Rejected by the producer, so not incurred.
- **Effect of the Q2 answer on this estimate:** negligible — moving
  `--needs-producer-review yes` inside the non-suppressed demotion branch and
  adding one cascade test is a sub-hour delta within the estimate's range; the
  figure above is unchanged.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-31 (plan re-run, session herdr-1793454596-4112787-24238).** Stage had
  been reset to `intake_complete` after the 2026-10-28 plan completion, so the
  plan was re-verified against current code and the 2026-10-29 recurrence
  evidence rather than re-decomposed. Conservative, intent-preserving edits:
  AC5 now also requires regression tests for the child exemption (AC6), the
  cascade-demotion-suppressed `No` → unchanged (Q2) and the
  `wl audit-show`-unavailable fail-safe; AC9 scoped explicitly to this
  repository (ContextHub `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` out of scope, per *Key Files*);
  a **Recurrence (2026-10-29)** note added to *Evidence*; SA-0MVTPAV4N005WPWF
  added to *Related work* as adjacent and out of scope. No children created
  (bug, complete implementation sketch, 0 children is the established shape for
  sibling audit-runner lifecycle items); no AC removed or reworded in intent;
  effort/risk re-confirmed unchanged.
- **2026-10-28 (intake + plan).** Producer answered Q1 = Option B+, Q2 = no,
  Q3 = yes; description updated with the *Review-state signal* decision and the
  cascade exception; plan auto-completed with 0 children.

## Problem

A full-project  run reports fixes that were never applied.

Observed on 2026-10-28 (SorraAgents @ dev):
- Report claimed `Auto-fixed: 8`, listing EXE005, ISC004, PLW1510 and RUF059 findings.
- `git status` afterwards showed **no source changes at all** (only the unrelated `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` scheduled-prompt timestamp).

Verified cause: those diagnostics are *not* auto-fixable (`ruff check --fix` reports `fix: null` for EXE005/PLW1510/RUF059 and `fix.applicability: unsafe` for ISC004).

## Root cause

`skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output` (line ~113) converts **every** diagnostic in ruff's JSON output into a `fixed_findings` entry, without inspecting `item['fix']` or `item['fix']['applicability']`. `auto_fix_files` (line ~217) then sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0` and the report prints those as auto-fixes. Ruff emits all diagnostics (fixed and unfixed) in its JSON output, so the count is the number of *diagnostics seen*, not fixes applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output` has the same shape (counts every message; eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields are ignored).

## Expected behaviour

- Only count a finding as auto-fixed when the linter actually applied an edit: ruff `item['fix']` is not `None` **and** `fix.applicability == 'safe'` (the default for `--fix` without `--unsafe-fixes`).
- Unfixable/unsafe diagnostics should either be dropped or surfaced as *remaining* smells, so they still reach smell detection, REFACTOR comments and work items.
- `fixes_applied`, the summary's `auto_fixed` count and the human-readable report must agree with what actually changed on disk.
- Add a regression test: a file with only-unsafe / no-fix diagnostics must report `Auto-fixed: 0`, and a file with a safe fix must report `Auto-fixed: 1` and be changed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output` only records findings whose fix is present and safe.
2. A full-project run against a tree whose only diagnostics are unsafe/unfixable reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A tree with one safe fix reports `Auto-fixed: 1` and the file is modified on disk.
4. Unsafe/unfixable diagnostics are still represented in the `Remaining smells` section (or equivalent) rather than silently dropped.
5. New unit tests in `skill/refactor/tests/` cover both cases.
6. Existing `skill/refactor` tests pass.

## Notes

Discovered from the `/skill:refactor` full-scan scheduled run. The 8 flagged diagnostics are already tracked by open REFACTOR items (SA-0MVRCL0Q90016C7D, SA-0MVRBPVU1001NGDW, SA-0MVRBPY7J004GJAI, SA-0MVPTU9HG00146UV), so this item is only about report/labelling accuracy.
data.title: refactor skill reports false auto-fixes for unfixable linter diagnostics

## Problem
`tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` spawns `process.env.PYTHON || "python3"` and exercises the real `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, which imports `numpy` (line 117). The repo declares no Python dependency manifest (no `requirements.txt`), so on a bare interpreter the whole unit node suite fails with `transcription failed: No module named 'numpy'` — the failure was red on this host from 2026-10-15 until numpy was installed ad hoc during the item above.

## Goal
As a maintainer, I want the voice-input worker's Python dependencies declared (and/or the unit test to skip with a clear message when they are absent), so a fresh checkout's full suite is green without undocumented host setup.

## Acceptance criteria
1. The worker's Python runtime dependencies (numpy, faster-whisper) are declared in a committed manifest (e.g. `pi-client/voice-input/requirements.txt`) and referenced from the voice-input README setup table.
2. `tests/unit/test-voice-whisper-worker.mjs` either documents the install step in its header or skips (with an explicit, non-silent message) when the resolved interpreter cannot import the required modules.
3. Full suite is green on an interpreter provisioned only from the committed manifest (verified via the test skill; no ad-hoc pip installs).

## Out of scope
Changing the worker's transcription behaviour or its stub-based test contract.

## Related
- SA-0MVRNLSQT006T5GQ — the test-failure item that surfaced this.
- LP-0MVO35BF90021QY6 — llm worklog item whose dev-push gate was blocked by it (code in SorraAgents).

## Goal

Five tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs` are source-code-grep / structural anti-patterns (per `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). Rework them to assert observable behaviour, or delete them if the behaviour is already covered elsewhere. Discovered by the test-churn pruning review (analyser v2.1.0, dev @ 7875214).

## Affected tests (line numbers at discovery)

- L427 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents the audit gating step` — reads SKILL.md text, asserts word substrings.
- L462 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js imports checkAuditReadyToClose` — reads source text, asserts string presence (the import behaviour is already exercised by the module-import behaviour tests).
- L478 `check-audit-gate: run-release.js uses exit code 6 for audit gate failure` — reads source text, asserts `'return 6'`/similar. Behaviour should be verified by exercising run-release against a failing audit gate.
- L496 `check-audit-gate: SKILL.md documents exit code 6 for audit gate` — includes a near-placeholder catch-all condition `(content.includes('6') && content.includes('audit'))` that matches almost any content.
- L865 `check-audit-gate: checkProducerReviewStatus has JSDoc comment` — structural-only test asserting documentation presence, not observable behaviour.

The file is otherwise healthy (89 tests, 255 asserts, real behaviour via `await import(MODULE_PATH)` + `execFileSync`); the fix must not remove the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The five tests above either pin observable behaviour (running the real module/gate and asserting output/exit codes) or are deleted.
- [ ] No test in the file reads a source or markdown file and asserts a substring of its text.
- [ ] The near-placeholder catch-all condition (L496) is eliminated.
- [ ] Behaviour previously pinned by each reworked test remains covered by a live test somewhere in the suite.
- [ ] Full suite passes after the change (run via the test skill).

## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report
